## v3.3 (2021-01-20)

Dragonboat v3.3 is a major release that comes with new features and improvements. All v3.2.x users are recommended to upgrade.

### New features

- Pebble, which is bidirectional compatible with RocksDB, has been made the default engine for storing Raft Logs. RocksDB and CGO are no longer required.
- Added the ability to slow down incoming proposals when the Raft Logs engine is highly loaded.
- Added the option to get notified when proposals and config changes are committed.
- Added a gossip service to allow NodeHosts to use dynamically assigned IP addresses as RaftAddress.
- Added the ability to better control memory footprint.
- Added ARM64/Linux as a new targeted platform.

Note that Pebble provides bidirectional compatibility with RocksDB v6.2.1. Existing Dragonboat applications can upgrade to v3.3 without any conversion unless a newer version of RocksDB was used. RocksDB v6.4.x has been briefly tested and it seems to be compatible with Pebble as well. 

### Improvements

- Optimized the read index implementation.
- Reduced LogDB restart delays.
- Made LogDB configurations accessible programmatically.
- Added protobuf workaround to allow Dragonboat and etcd to be used in the same project.
- Fixed a few data race issues.
- Fixed a potential Raft election deadlock issue when nodes are highly loaded.
- Allow incoming proposals to be rate limited when LogDB is busy.
- Simplified many aspects of the library.

### Breaking changes

- The signature of config.LogDBFactoryFunc has been changed. Your application is not affected unless it uses a custom LogDB implementation.
- Due to lack of user interests, C++ binding is no longer supported.
- LevelDB based LogDB is no longer supported.
- NodeHostConfig's FS and SystemTickerPrecision fields have been moved into NodeHostConfig.Expert.

## v3.2 (2020-03-05)

Dragonboat v3.2 comes with new features and improvements. All v3.1.x users are recommended to upgrade. 

### New features

- Added snappy compression support for Raft entries and snapshots.
- Added experimental witness support.
- Added new API to allow LogDB compaction to be manually triggered.
- Added event listener support to allow users to be notified for certain Raft events.
- Added system event listener support to allow users to be notified for certain system events.
- Added Raft related metrics to exported.
- Added rate limit support to control the maximum bandwidth used for snapshot streaming.
- Updated the C++ binding to cover all v3.1 features. Thanks JasonYuchen for working on that.
- Added a virtual filesystem layer to support more filesystem related tests.
- Added experimental Windows and FreeBSD support.

### Improvements

- Removed the restriction on max proposal payload size.
- Re-enabled the range delete support in LogDB.

managing its CPU, storage and network resources. Each NodeHost can manage Raft
nodes from many different Raft groups known as Raft clusters. Each Raft cluster
is identified by its ClusterID and it usually consists of multiple nodes, each
identified its NodeID value. Nodes from the same Raft cluster can be considered
as replicas of the same data, they are suppose to be distributed on different
NodeHost instances across the network, this brings fault tolerance to machine
and network failures as application data stored in the Raft cluster will be
available as long as the majority of its managing NodeHost instances (i.e. its
underlying hosts) are available.

User applications can leverage the power of the Raft protocol implemented in
dragonboat by implementing the IStateMachine or IOnDiskStateMachine component,
as defined in github.com/lni/dragonboat/v3/statemachine. Known as user state
machines, each IStateMachine and IOnDiskStateMachine instance is in charge of
updating, querying and snapshotting application data with minimum exposure to
the complexity of the Raft protocol implementation.

User applications can use NodeHost's APIs to update the state of their
IStateMachine or IOnDiskStateMachine instances, this is called making proposals.
Once accepted by the majority nodes of a Raft cluster, the proposal is
considered as committed and it will be applied on all member nodes of the Raft
cluster. Applications can also make linearizable reads to query the state of the
IStateMachine or IOnDiskStateMachine instances. Dragonboat employs the ReadIndex
protocol invented by Diego Ongaro for fast linearizable reads.

Dragonboat guarantees the linearizability of your I/O when interacting with the
IStateMachine or IOnDiskStateMachine instances. In plain English, writes (via
making proposal) to your Raft cluster appears to be instantaneous, once a write
is completed, all later reads (linearizable read using the ReadIndex protocol
as implemented and provided in dragonboat) should return the value of that write
or a later write. Once a value is returned by a linearizable read, all later
reads should return the same value or the result of a later write.

semantic required by linearizability. For a client, when it retries the proposal
that failed to complete before its deadline during the previous attempt, it has
the risk to have the same proposal committed and applied twice into the user
state machine. Dragonboat prevents this by implementing the client session
concept described in Diego Ongaro's PhD thesis.

Scope: captured tree `dbb02a05b62bbf7823fa3f8b5eb2ef9b949e6cc8`
(`github.com/lni/dragonboat/v3`, reports itself as v3.3.8 in
`nodehost.go:114-121`). Source is read-only; all work is in this directory.
Toolchain: go1.23.5, offline module cache. Ordinary shell has no network; tests
that listen on TCP were run through `isolated_exec`.

The reproduction tests are behind the `dragonboat_audit` build tag so the
default test run of the supplied code is unaffected. All commands below use
`-tags dragonboat_no_rocksdb,dragonboat_audit`.

Baseline evidence collected before any analysis:

- `go test -tags dragonboat_no_rocksdb -count=1 ./internal/...` passes except
  `internal/transport` (sandbox blocks `listen`, environmental) and
  `internal/logdb/tee` (rocksdb cgo header unavailable, environmental).
- `go test -tags dragonboat_no_rocksdb -count=1 .` (root package) passes.
- `go test -race -tags dragonboat_no_rocksdb -count=1 .` passes.
- Statement coverage: `internal/raft` 91.2%, root package 88.7%.

The upstream test suite therefore does not exercise the defects below.

## Summary

| ID | Region | Defect | Evidence |
|----|--------|--------|----------|
| F1 | `nodehost.go` `(*nodeUser).ReadIndex` | Enqueues a ReadIndex request without waking the execution engine; the request is only dispatched by the next tick. Up to one RTT added latency; a one-RTT timeout deterministically returns `RequestTimeout` on a healthy cluster, while `NodeHost.ReadIndex` with the same timeout completes. | Executed (5/5 failures), latency measurement, causality check in `audit/diag`. |
| F2 | `internal/raft/raft.go` `handleCandidateReadIndex` | The dropped ReadIndex is recorded twice, so `pb.Update.DroppedReadIndexes` contains the same `SystemCtx` twice for one request. Currently idempotent downstream; the raft update is wrong. | Executed. |

## Finding 1 (executed): `INodeUser.ReadIndex` never wakes the execution engine

Affected code: `nodehost.go`, `(*nodeUser).ReadIndex` (around line 2063).

```go
func (nu *nodeUser) ReadIndex(timeout time.Duration) (*RequestState, error) {
	return nu.node.read(nu.nh.getTimeoutTick(timeout))
}
```

Expected behavior. `GetNodeUser` returns an `INodeUser`; its `ReadIndex` doc
says "Its semantics is the same as the ReadIndex() method in NodeHost"
(`nodehost.go:2020-2038`). `NodeHost.ReadIndex` calls
`nh.engine.setStepReady(clusterID)` after enqueueing the request
(`nodehost.go:1477-1481`), and the sibling method `(*nodeUser).Propose` does the
same via its `setStepReady` field (`nodehost.go:2056-2060`). `nodeUser` even
holds `setStepReady` for this purpose (`nodehost.go:2040-2046`,
`GetNodeUser` at `nodehost.go:1383-1398`). A queued read-index request is
dispatched by `node.handleReadIndex()` from `handleEvents`, which only runs
when the cluster is marked step-ready.

What actually happens. Without the wakeup the request sits in
`pendingReadIndexes.requests` until the next step for that cluster. In an idle
cluster the next step is the tick worker (`NodeHost.tickWorkerMain` calls
`sendTickMessage` + `setAllStepReady` once per RTT,
`nodehost.go:1849-1876`). That is up to one RTT late, and the request deadline
is measured in the same RTT ticks (`getTimeoutTick`,
`pendingReadIndex.read`). A request whose timeout is one RTT
(`timeoutTick == 1`) therefore expires exactly when the next tick dispatches
it, and is completed with `requestTimeout`.

## Finding 2 (executed, minor): a candidate records a dropped ReadIndex twice

Affected code: `internal/raft/raft.go`, `(*raft).handleCandidateReadIndex`
(around line 1998).

```go
func (r *raft) handleCandidateReadIndex(m pb.Message) {
	plog.Warningf("%s dropped read index, no leader", r.describe())
	r.reportDroppedReadIndex(m)          // records ctx and publishes event
	ctx := pb.SystemCtx{Low: m.Hint, High: m.HintHigh}
	r.droppedReadIndexes = append(r.droppedReadIndexes, ctx) // records it again
}
```

Expected behavior. Each dropped request is reported once, as in the analogous
proposal path (`handleCandidatePropose` -> `reportDroppedProposal`) and the
follower/candidate request paths in general; `Update.DroppedReadIndexes` is the
list of dropped requests handed to the node layer.

What actually happens. One `ReadIndex` message delivered to a candidate
produces two identical `SystemCtx` entries in `r.droppedReadIndexes`, so every
`pb.Update` published for that step carries the request twice
(`Peer.getUpdate` copies the slice verbatim). The event/metric is published
once (`reportDroppedReadIndex`), so this is not double event reporting. The
node layer (`node.processDroppedReadIndexes` -> `pendingReadIndex.dropped`)
deletes the batch on the first call, so the duplicate is currently idempotent
there and clients are not notified twice; the observable defect is the
duplicated record in the raft update, i.e. the update does not represent the
one-dropped-request-per-message contract that the rest of the code follows.

--- PASS: TestAuditCandidateProposalIsDroppedOnce

consistent with the defect surviving it.

item.text:
I've completed this pass of the audit. Two concrete defects are reproduced on the unmodified captured source; the implementation itself is byte-identical to `../source` (only test files and notes were added).

**Finding 1 — `INodeUser.ReadIndex` never wakes the execution engine** ([nodehost.go](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_20-19-30-dragonboat_raft-baseline/work/nodehost.go:2063))

`(*nodeUser).ReadIndex` enqueues the request but, unlike `NodeHost.ReadIndex` (`nodehost.go:1477-1481`) and `(*nodeUser).Propose` (`nodehost.go:2056-2060`), it never calls `setStepReady`. The request is only dispatched by the next tick (once per RTT), so a one-RTT timeout deterministically returns `RequestTimeout` on a healthy cluster, while `NodeHost.ReadIndex` with the identical timeout completes. Measured with a longer timeout: ~10–60 µs via `NodeHost.ReadIndex` versus ~7–10 ms (one RTT) via `INodeUser.ReadIndex`.

Executed evidence: `TestAuditNodeUserReadIndexOneTickTimeout` failed 5/5; adding the single missing wakeup in an isolated copy (`audit/diag/`) makes the same test pass, confirming causality. The existing upstream test (`TestNodeHostNodeUserRead`, 45-RTT timeout) cannot see the delay.

**Finding 2 — a candidate records a dropped ReadIndex twice** ([raft.go](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_20-19-30-dragonboat_raft-baseline/work/internal/raft/raft.go:1998))

`handleCandidateReadIndex` calls `reportDroppedReadIndex` and then appends the same `SystemCtx` again, so `pb.Update.DroppedReadIndexes` carries two identical entries for one request. The node layer happens to be idempotent here (the batch is deleted on first handling), so no client double-notification results; the raft update is still wrong. This function has 0% statement coverage upstream.

Reproductions are preserved and gated behind the `dragonboat_audit` tag so the default suite is unaffected:

```
go test -tags dragonboat_no_rocksdb,dragonboat_audit -run TestAuditNodeUserReadIndexOneTickTimeout -v .
go test -tags dragonboat_no_rocksdb,dragonboat_audit -run TestAudit -v ./internal/raft/
```

The full write-up — expected behavior and basis, necessary conditions, executed outputs, non-findings (e.g. `Update.HasUpdate` ignoring `DroppedReadIndexes`, a cosmetic shadow in `transport.Chunk.record`), coverage data, and unresolved areas — is in [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_20-19-30-dragonboat_raft-baseline/work/report.md). Baseline context: the supplied v3.3.8 tree passes its own tests (root package, all internal packages that build offline) and `-race`; `internal/transport` and the rocksdb-backed packages could not be exercised in the ordinary shell for environmental reasons.
